Every one of the 380 results in a single 20 × 20 table. Read down a column for a club’s home record and across a row for its away record; the cell where the two meet carries the score, home side first. Each axis is set in the club’s own colour, and every cell is shaded by the home side’s result — green a home win, red a home defeat, charcoal a draw. Any score opens its matchweek.

Reading the scores

Scores are given home side first. On club pages the result is coloured from that club’s own point of view — green a win, charcoal a draw, red a defeat. Kick-off times are normalised to United Kingdom local time; the source records them against mixed UTC offsets.

Source and check

Results taken from the openfootball England dataset and reconciled in full against the published final table: all twenty clubs agree on played, won, drawn, lost, goal difference and points, and the goal differences sum to nought.

Final standings

League table

The completed 2025/26 table. Every column below is computed from the 380 results held in this file rather than transcribed, so the table and the results prove one another.

Arsenal finished seven points clear of Manchester City on 85 points, a fourth Premier League title. West Ham United, Burnley and Wolverhampton Wanderers were relegated. The twenty goal differences sum to nought, as they must.

Reading the scores

Scores are given home side first. On club pages the result is coloured from that club’s own point of view — green a win, charcoal a draw, red a defeat. Kick-off times are normalised to United Kingdom local time; the source records them against mixed UTC offsets.

Source and check

Results taken from the openfootball England dataset and reconciled in full against the published final table: all twenty clubs agree on played, won, drawn, lost, goal difference and points, and the goal differences sum to nought.

GoalkeeperDefenceMidfieldAttack

Appearances include substitute appearances — chained substitutions in the source are resolved in full — and won, drawn and lost are the club’s results in the matches each player featured in, so the three always sum to the appearance count. Goalkeeper and the defensive line are read directly from the recorded team-sheets and reflect where a man actually played. The sheets’ ordering of the midfield and forward lines is not dependable, so those two are assigned per club by calibration against 244 players of known position, who are themselves pinned to their true roles; a residual midfield–forward ambiguity remains possible among fringe players. Centre-back is not distinguished from full-back. A player who never started shows no position.

Age is as at 15 August 2025, the opening day. Nationality and age come from a separate open player database, not from the match record, and are shown only where the name matches a single player in it — 436 of 551 across the division. Where a name is shared by more than one footballer, or is absent, both fields are left blank rather than guessed. Unlike the appearance figures, neither column is reconciled against anything.

Appearances include substitute appearances — chained substitutions in the source are resolved in full — and won, drawn and lost are the club’s results in the matches each player featured in, so the three always sum to the appearance count. Goalkeeper and the defensive line are read directly from the recorded team-sheets and reflect where a man actually played. The sheets’ ordering of the midfield and forward lines is not dependable, so those two are assigned per club by calibration against 244 players of known position, who are themselves pinned to their true roles; a residual midfield–forward ambiguity remains possible among fringe players. Age is as at 15 August 2025, the opening day. Nationality and age come from a separate open player database, not from the match record, and are shown only where the name matches a single player in it — 436 of 551 across the division. Where a name is shared by more than one footballer, or is absent, both fields are left blank rather than guessed. Unlike the appearance figures, neither column is reconciled against anything.

The points
race

Every club’s running points total across the 38 rounds, each line in its own colour and labelled at the right-hand end. The lines begin together at nought and fan out; the steeper the line, the better the run of form. Where clubs finished level, their labels are nudged apart and a leader joins each back to its own line.

MW 22Arsenal

Horizontal axis is the matchweek · vertical axis is the running points total · shaded bands are alternate months · each line is labelled with its club’s three-letter code

The chart is drawn from the same 380 results as the rest of this file, on the same basis as the position grid: the total after rounds one to that matchweek complete. The column of labels is laid out at build time — each begins at the height of its line’s final value, then any that would overlap are pushed apart by the smallest amount that clears them, keeping their top-to-bottom order the same as the finishing order so that no leader line crosses another.

Ordered by final league position · a red rule marks the one club whose chairman changed during the season

Levy stepped down as executive chairman on 4 September 2025 after almost 25 years; Charrington took the newly created role of non-executive chairman. The club stated there was no change to ownership or shareholder structure. No club changed hands during the season. Arsenal had no chairman: the post has been vacant since 2020, with the club controlled by the Kroenke family through Kroenke Sports & Entertainment.

Chairmen are as recorded in the official Premier League Handbook for 2025/26, published in July 2025, which lists the officers of each club at the start of the season; the one subsequent change is shown alongside. Controlling entities and owner nationalities are drawn from club statements and press reporting. Ownership is often layered through holding companies and minority stakes, so the entity named is the one exercising control rather than a full account of the shareholding. None of this is derived from the match data or reconciled against it.

Rows are clubs · columns are months · each month is awarded to whoever held the post for the greater part of it

Interim or caretakerChange of manager

Because every bar is snapped to whole months, a spell too short to win a month is absorbed into the manager who did. Darren Fletcher’s eight days at Manchester United between Rúben Amorim and Michael Carrick, and Calum McFarlane’s first week at Chelsea before Liam Rosenior arrived, therefore do not appear as bars. Tenures are drawn from BBC Sport’s record of manager ins and outs and from the clubs’ own statements; unlike the results in this file they cannot be arithmetically reconciled.

Multi-year analysis

A decade of
points

The same ten seasons plotted against points rather than position. Seasons run left to right, oldest first; the scale runs from nought at the foot to 100 at the head. Every club sits at the exact total it finished on, so the height of a column — and the shaded envelope joining the best and worst of each year — is a true picture of how tightly or loosely that season’s twenty were packed. Champions are ringed in green and carry their figure.

Seasons run left to right, oldest first · the scale is labelled every ten points · the shaded band spans each season’s highest and lowest total · clubs level on points are set side by side at the same height

ChampionsNot yet played

No club is moved up or down to make room: every code is drawn at its exact points total, and where codes would collide they are spread sideways instead, in lanes centred on the season’s own axis. That keeps the vertical reading honest, which is the whole point of the chart. Clubs finished level on points 19 times across the nine seasons, and those pairs and trios appear side by side. Every figure is computed from that season’s 380 results, with the two points deductions of 2023/24 applied.

Premier League 2026/27 — a data annexe of aminbilal.com · Football.

Results and fixtures are drawn from the openfootball public-domain dataset and reconciled three ways before anything is shown: arithmetic self-consistency on every table, sourced club facts, and independent gates on eight completed seasons. Where a figure cannot be sourced, it is left blank rather than guessed.

Drafted with Claude Opus 5; web dress by Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic). Cookieless analytics by Plausible. Revised periodically through the season; each results page carries its last-revised date.
